challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: The observability pipeline is straining under the raw scan line volume, and the infrastructure bill has climbed sharply. I am prepared to drop the per till transaction logging to a daily aggregated summary per store. This reduces the data fidelity we capture for debugging edge cases, but it brings the compute and storage costs back within the approved budget envelope. If we accept losing that granular visibility, we can keep the core forecast service stable without triggering a new procurement cycle. I am comfortable with this reduction in logging detail to protect the overall system stability and stay within financial limits.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are prepared to give up granular logging detail (data fidelity) to accept the benefit of staying within budget and maintaining system stability.
